newsitem.title: IRAQ: More refugees leave Atrush camp in northern Iraq.
newsitem.headline: More refugees leave Atrush camp in northern Iraq.

text.p: The United Nations refugee agency UNHCR said on Tuesday that over 6,000 Turkish Kurdish refugees had abandoned a troubled camp in northern Iraq but UNHCR said it was concerned about those still there.

The Atrush camp, in Iraqi Kurdish controlled northern Iraq, at one time housed more than 14,000 refugees who fled their villages in southeast Turkey, where separatist Kurdish rebels are fighting Turkish troops.

But in January the United Nations pulled out of the camp, saying rebels from the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) had set up in the camp -- something Turkey had long asserted -- and were blocking aid work.

The UNHCR told refugees there it would help them if they left the camp or decided to return to Turkey. So far, 85 people have crossed back into Turkey, Ahmed Gubartalla, UNHCR's chief of mission in Iraq told Reuters.
Gubartalla said about 3,000 Turkish Kurds were now dispersed in make-shift encampments close to Dohuk and Harir, both in northern Iraq.
He said about 3,000 more had left for Ain Sifni, a government-controlled district on the fringes of the territory held by Iraqi Kurds since the 1991 Gulf War that drove Iraqi troops out of Kuwait.
"The Iraqi government has not yet admitted these people (as refugees). UNHCR is discussing the issue with the authorities to admit them on humanitarian grounds," Gubartalla said.

He said UNHCR had provided emergency supplies to everyone who left Atrush but had stop helping those still in the camp. But he said the agency's information showed the Kurds still in the camp were faring fine.

Diplomats in Baghdad said the people still in the camp were under pressure from rebels of the Kurdistan Democrartic Party (KDP) of Massoud Barzani, who with a rival group controls northern Iraq, to evacuate the camp.
"Turkey wants the camp dismantled and KDP has no option but to obey," said one diplomat.
